title: ASCEP Layer 4 — Measurement declaration and results
description: Layer 4 of the five ASCEP layers. SLO gates MUST be fixed here before the run (C7); gates chosen after seeing results make the sustainable tier meaningless. Every throughput figure MUST bind its input/output token counts (C4) and its topology (C3, inherited from the serving layer).

engine_version.description: Exact engine version at run time; restated here so a run record is self-contained (C8).

container_digest.description: Container digest actually executed (sha256); MUST match the serving declaration.

warmup_seconds.description: Seconds discarded before recording (warm-up). Units: seconds. Recording warm-up requests inflates TTFT tails and throughput variance.

warmup_seconds_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when warmup_seconds is null (C1).

repeats_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when repeats is null (C1).

sustained_window_seconds.description: Length of the sustained measurement window in seconds. SLO gates MUST hold for this full window for the point to count toward the sustainable tier.

sustained_window_seconds_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when sustained_window_seconds is null (C1).

concurrency_ladder.description: Concurrent-request levels applied, unitless. A single concurrency level cannot locate the binding floor.

outlier_method.description: Named outlier-handling method applied to raw records. 'none' is acceptable; undocumented trimming is a C8 failure.

open_loop.description: true if requests were submitted open-loop / saturation-style rather than user-paced. Open-loop runs measure engine ceiling, not user capacity; results MUST be labelled and MUST NOT populate the sustainable tier without user-pacing evidence.

ignore_eos.description: true if fixed-token ignore_eos generation was used. Such runs are engine-ceiling measurements and MUST NOT be reported as user capacity.

truncation_rate.description: Fraction of requests in the sustained window that stopped by hitting workload.max_output_tokens rather than emitting a stop token. REQUIRED by C4 alongside any throughput figure from a thinking or mixed workload. Measured at 0.464 on one thinking run: nearly half the generated tokens were real GPU work that delivered no answer, and a throughput figure that averages truncated and completed requests together overstates deliverable capacity by roughly that share.

slo_gates.description: Gate thresholds fixed BEFORE the run (C7). All gates MUST hold for the full sustained_window_seconds for a point to be SLO-passing.

ttft_p95_max_s.description: Time-to-first-token p95 gate, seconds. Null with reason permitted only if the workload genuinely has no TTFT requirement.

ttft_p95_max_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification for a null ttft gate.

itl_p95_max_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification for a null ITL gate.

e2e_p95_max_s.description: End-to-end request latency p95 gate, seconds.

e2e_p95_max_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification for a null e2e gate.

declared_before_run.description: MUST be true (C7). false makes the report non-conforming.

error_rate_max_pct_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when error_rate_max_pct is null (C1).

environment_capture_path.description: Relative path to captured environment (versions, topology, knobs) in the reproduction bundle (C8).

raw_records_path.description: Relative path to per-request raw records (C8). Aggregate tables without raw records are non-conforming.

engine_logs_path.description: Relative path to engine logs, including the startup line printing the KV cache size.

results.description: One entry per (shape, concurrency) point. At least three distinct context lengths SHOULD be present (C4); fewer MUST be labelled with `single_point`.

allOf.$comment: A reported ITL percentile whose population is null is exactly the unlabelled figure §4.1 forbids: pooled-gaps and per-request-mean have different tails, so the reader cannot recompute it.

A pooled-gaps row asserts that each streamed chunk carried one decode step, and only tokens_per_stream_chunk can support that: where a server coalesces, the pooled 'ITL' tail is an inter-chunk tail wearing an inter-token name and can be an order of magnitude high. On the H100 rehearsal the undeclared substitution moved sustainable capacity from 2,503 tok/s to 1,180 tok/s. The row may still say the factor is unknown, but it must say something -- an unsupported pooled percentile that is silently accepted is the whole defect. Rows on the per-request population owe nothing here: their denominator is the server's own token count, which no transport can inflate.

slo_pass grades the pooled window while outcome fails the rung on any single failing repetition, so one row can legitimately carry slo_pass: true beside outcome: 'failed'; published without the grading sentences, that pair reads as a harness contradiction and the boundary it asserts is unexplained.

input_tokens.description: Mean input tokens per request at this point (C4). Units: tokens.

output_tokens.description: Mean output tokens per request at this point (C4). Units: tokens.

peak_in_flight.description: The most requests simultaneously open during the selected window (M), swept from the raw records as half-open [issued_ts, end_ts) intervals over in-window traffic only. This is what the rung ACHIEVED, against `concurrency`, which is what it DECLARED. The two are not the same figure and the gap is load-bearing: under a closed loop with think time the peak sits legitimately below the declared value by roughly the duty cycle, but a peak that stops tracking the declaration and pins at a constant across several rungs is a throttle, not a saturation point. This project shipped three campaigns reporting a measured 128 concurrent users before noticing that its own HTTP client defaulted to a 100-connection pool, so every rung above 100 offered exactly 100 while throughput flatlined and the knee looked real. Nothing in a bundle could have revealed it, which is why the figure is recorded rather than inferred. Optional: reports published before the diagnostic existed do not carry it, and its absence means the run was not checked, never that it passed.

ttft_p95_s.description: TTFT p95, seconds (M). Capacity is set by the tail; means MUST NOT substitute.

itl_p50_s.description: Inter-token latency p50, seconds (M). Population declared by itl_population.

itl_p95_s.description: Inter-token latency p95, seconds (M). Population declared by itl_population.

itl_population.description: Which ITL distribution the itl_p* figures were computed over (§4.1): one sample per streamed chunk across the window, or one sample per request. The two have different tails and different sample counts, so an unlabelled percentile is not reproducible. Where the server coalesced decode steps into one chunk the first is not inter-token latency at all, so tokens_per_stream_chunk decides which population a measured row may use (§4.4). Null only when every itl_p* is null.

tokens_per_stream_chunk.description: Output tokens per streamed content chunk over this window: server-reported output tokens summed over the usable records, divided by their summed chunk counts, so the window's whole token population speaks rather than a mean of per-request ratios. A value above 1 means the server coalesced several decode steps into one SSE delta, and past the switch point of 1.05 -- a tolerance band around the exact 1.0 a genuinely per-token stream measures, wide enough to absorb the occasional double-packed delta -- the itl_p* figures MUST be computed per request rather than per gap (§4.4), because pooled gaps between chunks are then inter-chunk latencies wearing an inter-token name, and a finer sample of the wrong quantity is still the wrong quantity. Measured at 6.65 on the concurrency-128 rung of the H100 rehearsal, where the two populations' p95 read 0.2953 s and 0.0247 s against a declared 0.05 s ITL gate. Null only when no usable record carried both per-token stamps and a usage count.

stream_chunk_gap_p50_s.description: p50 of the gaps between streamed content chunks, seconds -- what the client observed at the transport, one sample per chunk however many decode steps the server folded into it. Published under a name that is not ITL because it is not ITL, and published whenever per-token stamps exist rather than only on divergence: a field that appears only when something went wrong is a field nobody builds a comparison on. It coincides with itl_p50_s wherever tokens_per_stream_chunk sits below the coalescing switch and parts from it exactly where the server coalesced, so the divergence on a row is the substitution made visible.

stream_chunk_gap_p95_s.description: p95 of the gaps between streamed content chunks, seconds -- the transport-side tail that a pooled "ITL p95" would otherwise reprint under the wrong name: 0.2953 s at the H100 rehearsal's concurrency-128 rung where the per-request ITL p95 was 0.0247 s. A smoothness SLO written against what the client actually sees is legitimately gated on this figure; it is simply not the ITL figure, and itl_population says which distribution itl_p95_s itself came from.

output_tok_s.description: Aggregate OUTPUT tokens/s for the full window (M), at this shape, concurrency, and topology only. Never topology- or context-independent (C3/C4). Feeds ascep.capacity.capacity_at(throughput_tok_s=...).

output_tok_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when output_tok_s is null (C1).

prefill_tok_s.description: Aggregate PROMPT tokens/s for the full window (M), computed from the same raw records, window and repetition selection that produced output_tok_s, at this shape, concurrency and topology only. Never topology- or context-independent (C3/C4). Units: tokens/s. Feeds ascep.capacity.capacity_at(prefill_tok_s=...). output_tok_s prices decode alone while the workload layer already charges prompt tokens to KV memory, so without this figure prefill compute is the one axis with no floor. Null while a capacity number is published triggers the C11 warning.

prefill_tok_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when prefill_tok_s is null (C1). Hard to sustain: the raw records already carry per-request input token counts and timestamps, so a null asserts the records were discarded, not that the observable was unavailable to the harness.

measured_input_output_ratio.description: Prompt tokens per generated token over the same window as output_tok_s and prefill_tok_s: summed input tokens divided by summed output tokens across the usable records, so the window's whole token population speaks rather than a mean of per-request ratios. Unitless. This is the mix the throughput figures were measured at. The prefill floor binds exactly when the declared workload's input:output ratio exceeds it, and without this field the C11 overstatement factor is not computable, so a benchmark taken on a generation-heavy mix passes silently against an input-heavy deployment.

measured_input_output_ratio_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when measured_input_output_ratio is null (C1). Common for legacy campaigns that logged context length but not the input/output split.

gpu_util_pct.description: Mean device utilization over the window, percent (M).

gpu_mem_util_pct.description: Peak device memory utilization over the window, percent (M).

error_rate_pct.description: Failed-request rate over the window, percent (M).

slo_pass.description: true iff every gate held for the full window. Feeds ascep.capacity.capacity_at(slo_pass=...); a passing-floors run with slo_pass=false binds at Constraint.SLO.

dispersion.description: Dispersion across the rung's counted repetitions (C8): minimum, lower median and maximum of the four figures the SLO gate reads plus throughput -- the figures a reader sizes from and the figures a gate verdict turns on. Null with dispersion_u_reason when the rung had fewer than two counted repetitions, because a block of identical min, median and max would publish perfect stability as a finding when nothing was measured twice. Optional so reports written before chapter 7 required it still validate; a fresh harness report that omits the key is a C12 violation, not a rung with nothing to say.

repetitions_counted.description: How many counted repetitions the rung had. The section 5 confirmation window is excluded, exactly as the row itself excludes it.

ttft_p95_s.description: Spread of ttft_p95_s across the counted repetitions. Null with ttft_p95_s_u_reason when no counted repetition produced the figure.

median.description: Lower median: index (n - 1) // 2 of the sorted values, the same convention as the row picker, so the two cannot drift into meaning different things.

n.description: How many counted repetitions produced this figure. It can be less than repetitions_counted: a window whose reduction could not compute a tail leaves it null, and a min/max over the survivors that claimed three would report a narrower spread than the rung actually had.

spread_pct.description: (max - min) / median * 100, rounded to two decimals. Null with spread_pct_u_reason when the median is zero -- a relative spread against a zero median is a division by zero dressed as a statistic.

itl_p95_s.description: Spread of itl_p95_s across the counted repetitions. Null with itl_p95_s_u_reason when no counted repetition produced the figure.

dispersion_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when dispersion is null (C12): says how many counted repetitions the rung actually had.

outcome.description: Closed outcome vocabulary for this ladder rung (chapter 7 §7). 'failed' is a real result — capacity ends here; 'invalid' is a defective measurement and is not a result at all. slo_pass alone conflates the two, which lets a true system limit be laundered into an instrumentation excuse and a broken harness into a capacity boundary.

reasons.description: The grader's own record of why this rung is not COMPLETE: full sentences, in grading order, each naming the repetition or boundary test that failed and the section that requires the verdict. REQUIRED whenever outcome is 'failed' or 'invalid'. §5 fails a rung on any single failing repetition while slo_pass grades the pooled window, so the two keys answer different questions, and a row that asserts both without the sentence that produced the verdict hands the reader a capacity boundary with no stated cause, to be re-derived by hand from the raw records.

outcome_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when outcome is null (C1).

provenance.description: Row-level provenance tag (C2). Rows in the results table SHOULD be 'M'; anything else requires justification in §7 of the report.

context_tokens.description: Context length this point was measured at (C4), tokens. Either this or input_tokens/output_tokens MUST be present: a throughput figure with no context length attached is not a measurement of anything.

context_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when context_tokens is null (C1).

input_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when input_tokens is null (C1). Common for legacy campaigns that logged context length but not the input/output split.

output_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when output_tokens is null (C1). Common for legacy campaigns that logged context length but not the input/output split.

concurrency_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when concurrency is null (C1). Common for legacy campaigns that logged context length but not the in-flight request count.

items.description: A measured operating point. It MUST be identifiable in context: either context_tokens or input_tokens must carry a real value.

single_point.description: True when this campaign measured fewer than three distinct context lengths. C4 requires a single point be labelled as such: without this field the same three rows read as a curve, and a reader projects a figure to a shape it was never measured at. Setting it does not raise the report's grade -- it states the limit the grade already reflects.

engine_version_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when engine_version is null (C1).

container_digest_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when container_digest is null (C1).

outlier_method_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when outlier_method is null (C1).

percentile_method.description: Named percentile interpolation convention used to compute every p50/p95/p99 in this run, e.g. 'hyndman-fan-type-7'. Chapter 4.3 makes type-7 the protocol default; a run using anything else must say so, because two conventions give different tails from identical records and the difference lands in an SLO gate.

percentile_method_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when percentile_method is null (C1).

tokenizer.description: Identifier of the tokenizer used for the independent local token count required by chapter 4.7.1, e.g. a HuggingFace repo id plus revision. Without it the server-vs-tokenizer reconciliation cannot be reproduced, and an undetected fertility mismatch moves every context-length and KV figure in the report.

tokenizer_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when tokenizer is null (C1).

drain_deadline_seconds.description: Grace period in seconds after measurement-window close within which a straddling request may still complete and count as a valid latency sample. Chapter 7 §6 requires it because without it a late finisher is simultaneously a valid tail sample and a non-completion, and the harness resolves that contradiction whichever way flatters the run.

drain_deadline_seconds_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when drain_deadline_seconds is null (C1).

throughput_collapse_ratio.description: Fixed ratio r_c, declared before timing, below which a rung's throughput relative to the best lower complete rung counts as throughput collapse and terminates the ladder (chapter 7 §7). Throughput, not goodput: collapse is a queueing failure a rung can suffer whether or not its gates held, and goodput is undefined at a rung that failed them. MUST NOT be below 0.5. Left to operator taste after the fact, 'collapse' becomes whatever keeps the ladder climbing.

throughput_collapse_ratio_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when throughput_collapse_ratio is null (C1).

monotonic_across_ladder.description: Whether pass/fail outcomes were monotone across the measured concurrency ladder (chapter 7 §5). A bisection over a non-monotone function returns an arbitrary point wearing a boundary label, so a reader needs to know which of the two they are looking at.

monotonic_across_ladder_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when monotonic_across_ladder is null (C1).
